useUpstreamCatalog.title: Use the MobilityData GOFS registry
useUpstreamCatalog.description: On by default. Reads the community-maintained systems.json from the GOFS repository so newly published on-demand systems appear without a config change. Each entry is checked before it is offered: unreachable feeds are hidden, and feeds that need an API key are shown with a link to the operator's access page. Turn off to use only the feeds listed below.

feeds.title: Additional GOFS feeds
feeds.description: On-demand transport feeds published in the General On-Demand Feed Specification (GOFS 1.0), added on top of the upstream registry — or instead of it. Use this for a feed the registry does not list yet, or a private deployment. Point 'url' at the feed's discovery document; note that many feeds serve it at a bare base URL rather than a path ending in gofs.json. Service areas, brands, fares and booking links are read from the feed itself. An entry here overrides an upstream one with the same id.

id.title: Feed id
id.description: Short stable identifier, e.g. montreal-taxi. Becomes the provider id gofs-<id>.

name.title: Display name
name.description: Shown in the ride panel until the feed's own system name loads.

url.title: Discovery URL
url.description: Absolute https URL of the feed's discovery document. Often a bare base URL such as https://api.example.com/gofs/11 rather than a path ending in gofs.json.

credentialSlot.title: API key slot
credentialSlot.description: Only for a feed that needs an API key. Pick a slot (1-3) and paste the key into the matching 'Custom GOFS feed N API key' field below. The key is stored encrypted; the settings here are not secret.

authKind.title: How the key is sent
authKind.description: Send the key as an HTTP header (default, preferred — a key in a query string ends up in access logs) or as a query parameter.

authParam.title: Header or parameter name
authParam.description: The name the feed expects, e.g. X-API-KEY for a header or api_key for a query parameter. Defaults to X-API-KEY.

ca-taxi-montreal-api-key.title: Taxi Montréal API key
ca-taxi-montreal-api-key.description: Unlocks the Montreal Taxi Registry GOFS feed (~3,300 taxis), which the registry lists publicly but serves only to keyed callers. Leave empty to skip it; every other feed works without a key.

steps: Open the Registre des taxis technical documentation and read the operator guide (the deep-link approach) to see which endpoints your deployment will call.
Develop against the acceptance environment, which the documentation describes.
Contact the registry administrator via the 'Nous joindre' page to have your integration verified.
The administrator issues a production API key once the integration is confirmed. Paste it here.
x-openmapx-setup.cost: No published price; access is granted by the registry administrator.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: The key is sent as an X-API-KEY request header. The published guide is written for taxi dispatch operators, so a consuming application should say so explicitly when making contact.

gofs-custom-1-api-key.title: Custom GOFS feed 1 API key
gofs-custom-1-api-key.description: API key for a feed you added above with 'API key slot' set to 1. Stored encrypted and sent only to that feed.

gofs-custom-2-api-key.title: Custom GOFS feed 2 API key
gofs-custom-2-api-key.description: API key for a feed you added above with 'API key slot' set to 2. Stored encrypted and sent only to that feed.

gofs-custom-3-api-key.title: Custom GOFS feed 3 API key
gofs-custom-3-api-key.description: API key for a feed you added above with 'API key slot' set to 3. Stored encrypted and sent only to that feed.
